item.title: Translating Wearable Ultrasound with System Integration and Enabling Technologies
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 24 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00118-z

Wearable ultrasound systems enable continuous, non-invasive sensing for biomedical monitoring and human–machine interaction. Despite rapid technological progress, most implementations remain confined to laboratory prototypes. We argue that open, modular platforms are key to bridging this gap, enabling application-oriented research, lowering interdisciplinary entry barriers, and supporting the translation of wearable ultrasound from experimental systems toward manufacturable designs.

item.title: Sensing Complex Lipids in Sweat Continuously
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 21 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00130-3

A wearable patch continuously monitors cholesterol and triglycerides in sweat to track personalized metabolic responses to diet and exercise.

item.title: High-Performance Gas Sensors Through Predictive Material Design
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 21 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00115-2

Progress in high-performance gas sensors is limited by complex gas–surface interactions and trial-and-error discovery; this Perspective proposes a predictive twin-loop framework that integrates single-atom materials, operando analysis and machine learning to enable mechanism-guided design with improved response, selectivity and stability.

item.title: A Bimodal Sensor with Deep Learning-Enhanced Synergistic Sensing for Intelligent Recognition and Navigation
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 20 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00127-y

A bio-inspired flexible bimodal sensor integrates co-located photoelectric and pressure sensing with decoupled outputs, enabling high-accuracy object recognition, autonomous robotic navigation and precision agricultural monitoring via synergistic data fusion.

item.title: Direct Light-To-Token Conversion with Integrated 2D Photosensitive Memory
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 19 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00122-3

A large-scale 2D photosensitive memory array enables direct image-to-token conversion for visual transformers, reducing energy consumption while preserving software-level accuracy.

item.title: Time to Standardize Event-Based Vision Processing
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 17 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00100-9

A decade of event-based vision research has produced sensors that offer clear advantages over conventional imagers in temporal resolution, dynamic range, and power consumption. What it has not yet produced is the shared calibration, processing, and metadata conventions that would make those sensors deployable at scale.

item.title: Three Stacked Layers for Autonomous Sensing
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 04 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00125-0

Three stacked layers for autonomous sensing

item.title: Multimodal Monitoring of a Seafloor Spreading Event
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 04 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00124-1

Multimodal monitoring of a seafloor spreading event

item.title: Bistable Haptic Textiles for Immersive Somatosensory Augmentation and Sensory Substitution
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 03 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00120-5

A textile-based bistable soft-pneumatic haptic interface enables full-body multimodal tactile feedback for immersive virtual environments, tactile communication and assistive sensory substitution applications.

item.title: A Neuromorphic Bionic Eye with Ultradense Waveguide-Coupled Pixels for Depth-Tunable 3D Vision
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00119-y

A neuromorphic bionic eye with ultradense waveguide-coupled pixels and depth-adaptive optics enables high-fidelity 3D imaging and motion tracking for next-generation bio-inspired vision systems.

item.title: All-Wave Computational Ultrasonic Fingerprint Identification with Metasurface-Driven Loop-Diffractive Neural Network
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 31 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00102-7

In-sensor spatial decoding enables single-step physical computation for fingerprint recognition, removing stored templates and delivering efficient, wave-based biometric authentication.

item.title: Complementary Stretchable Amplifiers for Stable Biosignal Recording
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00094-4

Stretchable complementary transistor amplifiers maintain stable gain under strain, enabling motion-robust, high-fidelity biosignal recording in soft bioelectronic interfaces.

item.title: Elastic in Vivo Biosignal Amplifiers Based on Strain-Insensitive Material and Circuit Design
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 30 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00091-7

Elastic organic electrochemical transistor amplifiers deliver strain-insensitive, high-gain in vivo signal amplification with a good signal-to-noise ratio through an integrated materials–device–circuit design.

item.title: Binding Assays First, Then Biosensors
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 29 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00092-6

Biosensors rely on biomolecular interactions for detection, and rigorous binding assays must therefore precede biosensor development. Conflating these two distinct measurements risks mischaracterizing biomolecules and propagating errors throughout subsequent biosensor design and interpretation.

item.title: Field-Deployable Full-Range Underwater pH Sensor Using a Polyprotic SERS Probe
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 29 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00107-2

A fibre-optic surface-enhanced Raman scattering pH sensor based on a polyprotic probe enables accurate underwater measurements across the full pH range and demonstrates stability and robustness for environmental monitoring under extreme conditions.

item.title: Non-Invasive Continuous Lipid Profiling via Cofactor-Refreshing Cascading Enzymatic Reactions and Causal Machine Learning
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 29 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00117-0

A cofactor-refreshing wearable lipid sensor continuously measures cholesterol and triglycerides in sweat, enabling long-term lipid tracking and supporting personalized lipid analysis with causal machine learning.

item.title: Attention-Driven In-Sensor Selective Computing
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 27 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00114-3

A butterfly-inspired polarization-sensitive vision sensor enables selective in-sensor processing and feature-specific imaging for accurate object recognition in cluttered environments with improved efficiency.

item.title: A Vision Sensor that Programs Its Own Timescales
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00106-3

A phototransistor that couples fast charge trapping with slow ferroelectric polarization turns photocarrier lifetime from a fixed material parameter into a programmable hardware variable, enabling one sensor array to adapt its visual memory to motion across three orders of magnitude in speed.

item.title: Computing the Rainbow at the Source
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 23 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00111-6

A voltage-tunable photodiode paired with a programmable analog readout collapses spectral encoding and decoding into a single sensor-level operation, enabling wavelength reconstruction and task-ready recognition without exporting raw photocurrents.

item.title: Intelligent Sensing Is Reshaping Personalized Food Safety
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 21 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00099-z

Consumer-deployable sensing promises personalized food safety risk prediction but also exposes deep vulnerabilities in robustness, privacy, equity and governance. As intelligent sensing moves from the laboratory to the kitchen, society must confront who benefits, who is protected and who is left behind.

item.title: Embodied Sensorimotor Arm Helps Robot Adapt to Dynamic Environments
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00112-5

A robotic arm is developed that integrates a rigid skeleton with soft tactile skin to achieve human-like, whole-arm touch perception. This embodied sensorimotor system — EmArm — enables real-time physical adaptation, including stable contact-rich manipulation and safe trajectory replanning in dynamic, unstructured environments.

item.title: Embodied Sensorimotor Integration for Whole-Arm Tactile Sensing and Adaptive Robotic Manipulation
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00097-1

A rigid–soft robotic arm integrates large-area tactile skins, proprioception and closed-loop control to achieve real-time high-resolution whole-arm sensing, human intent recognition and adaptive manipulation in dynamic, contact-rich complex environments.

item.title: AI-Powered Closed-Loop Wearable Bioelectronics for Personalized and Autonomous Healthcare
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00105-4

Artificial intelligence-powered closed-loop wearable bioelectronics integrates multimodal sensing, adaptive algorithms and therapeutic intervention to enable autonomous, personalized care. This Review discusses hardware advances, system integration, reliability and translational challenges to outline pathways towards safe, scalable and clinically deployable intelligent healthcare systems.

item.title: Synergistic Material–algorithm Design Enables Robust Auditory Attention Decoding Brain–computer Interface Applications
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00103-6

An oxidant-free oligomer-based zwitterionic hydrogel electrode and an ultra-lightweight spiking transformer algorithm enable high-fidelity, low-power auditory attention decoding for practical wearable brain–computer interface applications.

item.title: Brain-Inspired Visual Sensing–perception for Open-World Environments
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00095-3

A brain-inspired two-stage sensing–perception framework couples bottom-up visual priors with top-down adaptive modulation, enabling robust open-world vision under extreme real-world degradations.

item.title: A Spike–language Dual Framework Bridges Fast Perception and Deep Reasoning in Artificial Tactile Somatosensory Systems
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00108-1

Spike–language dual encoding integrates tactile sensors with spiking neural networks and large language models to enhance robotic perception and cognition in object classification and semantic reasoning, bridging gaps in tactile processing.

item.title: Temporal Programmable In-Sensor System for Multi-Speed Motion Perception
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00101-8

A temporally programmable in-sensor system using ferroelectric–charge trapping transistors enables multi-speed motion perception with wide tunable dynamics, low crosstalk and scalable arrays for efficient real-time analysis in dynamic environments.

item.title: Clarifying the Landscape of Mechanical Sensors from Stress to Strain
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00090-8

Stress and strain sensors underpin mechanical sensing across electronics, robotics and bioengineering, yet their distinct physical meanings and response pathways are often confused. This Review establishes a unifying, mechanics-based framework that clarifies stress- versus strain-driven sensing, guiding rational device design, performance evaluation and application-specific sensor selection.

item.title: Ten Questions on the Future of Sensing
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00093-5

As sensing technologies become increasingly multi- and inter-disciplinary, their role is rapidly evolving beyond signal detection. In this Viewpoint, five experts discuss emerging sensing paradigms, ethical and societal challenges, and the system-level innovations needed to translate laboratory breakthroughs into robust, trustworthy technologies for real-world deployment.

item.title: High-Fidelity Dispersive Spin Sensing in a Tunable Unit Cell of Silicon MOS Quantum Dots
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00084-6

A compact, industrially fabricated single electron box sensor enables state-of-the-art high-fidelity dispersive spin readout within a tunable silicon MOS quantum dot unit cell.

item.title: A Self-Powered Capsule for Drinking Water Safety
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00110-7

A self-powered capsule for drinking water safety

item.title: High-Resolution Tracking of Global Tree Cover Loss Drivers
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00113-4

High-resolution tracking of global tree cover loss drivers

item.title: Shaping the AI Systems that Speak for Science
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 07 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00109-0

Researchers are increasingly discovering and consuming scientific knowledge through artificial intelligence (AI) platforms built by technology companies. Here we discuss what publishers and editors can do to co-create use-cases and governance of the AI systems that mediate science.

item.title: Improved Perception for Machine Vision Under Complex Illumination
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 01 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00104-5

Optical interference from lasers and intense lighting can confuse machine vision. Now, a tunable band-stop photodetector has been designed that uses machine learning to suppress disruptive spectral components at the sensor, enabling more reliable perception in challenging illumination.

item.title: Tunable Band-Stop Photodetection with Machine Learning-Enabled Broadband Spectral Adaptation
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 01 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00098-0

A machine learning-guided tunable band-stop photodetector enables adaptive suppression of unpredictable light interference for robust broadband machine vision.

item.title: AI Clones in Conversation at Academic Conferences
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00089-1

Artificial intelligence (AI) clones could serve as a new interface for scientific communication between publishers and research communities. At a Nature conference in Seoul, multimodal AI clones — including one of the Chief Editor of Nature Sensors — engaged researchers in real-time dialogue about publishing and careers, in three different languages.

item.title: Non-Contact Biomechanical Profiling of 3D Tissues
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00096-2

A wireless biomechanical sensing platform enables non-contact, scalable, cost-effective profiling of three-dimensional (3D) cardiac organoids and engineered heart tissues.

item.title: Wireless and Contactless Biomechanic Well Plate for Monitoring Cardiac Organoid and 3D-Tissue Contraction
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 26 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00087-3

A wireless and contactless biomechanical well plate leverages ultrasensitive silicon cantilevers to enable high-throughput, real-time quantification of contractile forces in cardiac organoids and engineered heart tissues.

item.title: Integrated Thermal Sensing of Vascular Morphology for Haemodynamic Monitoring
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 12 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00082-8

A wearable thermal sensing approach enables non-invasive inference of vascular depth and diameter from skin thermal transients, improving the accuracy of haemodynamic modelling.

item.title: In-Sensor Spectral Decoding for Efficient Spectroscopic Recognition
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 12 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00085-5

In-sensor spectral decoding enables direct spectral reconstruction and application-level recognition without off-chip computation, delivering efficient spectroscopic sensing.

item.title: Multiparametric Molecular Imaging of the Brain
item.description:
Nature Sensors, Published online: 09 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s44460-026-00088-2

Multiparametric molecular imaging of the brain
